# PREFIX-852 — Partial-baseline named BRC resynchronization: exact uncertainty-coordinate criterion

Date: 2026-11-17. Status: AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_FINITE_REGRESSION / NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED.
Frozen scientific input: \`f42f2906d77f24085c123f3ccfe9667d41caa96d\`. Scientific dependency: PREFIX-847–851, especially PREFIX-851 (fully known old state). Researcher/source lineage: EM-DIRECT-B518B3, RA-14044F2E842D112941E256BF. Independent auxiliary research; no shared X6 task CLAIM.

## 1. Typed model and question

The auxiliary positive-integer Q-only, provenance-*named* BRC observer has p named sources, each with binary increment x_i in {0,1}, and encoded current state

    U(x) = sum_{i=0}^{p-1} 2^i x_i,   0 <= U < N=2^p.

This is an exact observer coding of the declared named weight vector, not a native Cell/Link/Port state identification. A known fixed baseline S_0 is added. At observation time t, after r>=0 missing one-source-at-most update steps, the measurement is

    Y_t(x) = c_t (S_0+U(x)) mod q,  c_t=2^{floor(t/2)}, q>=3 odd.

The receiver knows the old bits **outside** a specified set J subset {0,...,p-1}. The old values on J are unknown, and each of the r steps can flip at most one coordinate (or do nothing). Recovery must work for *every* assignment to the known old bits and unknown old bits. The observation time t and q are known. There is no requirement that the receiver know which bits actually changed.

Write K=J^c, s=|J|, k=|K|. For a known old assignment z_K, the set of *possible current states* is exactly

    R(z_K;J,r)={x in {0,1}^p : Hamming(x_K,z_K)<=r}.       (1)

**Proof:** any reachable x differs from the true old state in at most r coordinates, hence on K in at most r coordinates. Conversely choose the unknown old J-bits equal to x_J, flip the at-most-r differing K-bits and insert no-ops. This establishes equality. In particular all J-bit values are still legitimate and their provenance cannot be erased.

## 2. Uniform exact no-alias theorem

For each signed coefficient vector epsilon_i in {-1,0,+1}, not identically zero, whose support on K has size at most 2r, define

    d(epsilon)=|sum_{i=0}^{p-1} epsilon_i 2^i| .

Define D(p,J,r) as the set of all such d. These integers are nonzero by dominance of the highest nonzero binary positional term over all lower terms. Also d < 2^p.

**THEOREM 852-A (necessary and sufficient).** A fixed odd q>=3 permits recovery of the complete named current state, uniformly for every old known assignment z_K and every admissible r-missed-step history, iff

    forall d in D(p,J,r),   d mod q != 0.                   (2)

The exact minimal allowed modulus is

    q*(p,J,r) = min { odd q>=3 : forall d in D(p,J,r), q does not divide d } .   (3)

Its output-port width is ceil(log2 q*). The receiver additionally stores the k known old bits, the set J, time/parameter information and decoder; port width alone is not full system memory.

**Proof.** Because q is odd, c_t is invertible modulo q. Subtract S_0 after inversion, so two current states alias exactly when q divides U(x)-U(y). Their signed binary difference has coefficient epsilon_i=x_i-y_i, hence support precisely the coordinates at which x and y differ.

Fix any K-old assignment z_K. Two states x,y lie in R(z_K;J,r) exactly when both K-projections are within r of z_K. Across all possible z_K, such a common anchor exists iff Hamming(x_K,y_K)<=2r. Necessity follows from the triangle inequality; for sufficiency, split the coordinates where x_K and y_K disagree into two sets of size at most r, and choose z_K to match one candidate on one set and the other on the complement. J coordinates impose no constraint on this anchor. Thus a collision for some allowed old assignment is *equivalent* to q dividing a nonzero signed binary difference with at most 2r nonzeros in K. This is (2); (3) follows by minimization. QED.

The formula specializes to PREFIX-851 when J is empty.

## 3. Information bound, saturation and exact zero-erasure law

**THEOREM 852-B (tight universal information bound).** Every feasible q satisfies

    q >= V(p,J,r) := 2^s sum_{j=0}^{min(r,k)} C(k,j).       (4)

Also q*(p,J,r)<=2^p+1. If 2r>=k, then the exact answer is

    q*(p,J,r)=2^p+1.                                      (5)

**Proof.** (1) contains V distinct states for every fixed z_K; one residue must distinguish each, proving (4). The odd integer N+1>N separates every U in [0,N-1]. If 2r>=k, every pair x,y has K-Hamming distance <=2r, so (2) requires the map U mod q be injective on all N consecutive integers. Thus q>=N, and since N=2^p is even, the smallest permitted odd q is N+1. QED.

**THEOREM 852-C (contiguous uncertain block at zero erasures).** If r=0 and J={a,a+1,...,a+s-1}, s>=1, with a+s<=p, then

    q*(p,J,0)=2^s+1,                                      (6)

independent of the block's position a.

**Proof.** All candidate current encodings have the form B+2^a v, with v in [0,2^s-1] and B fixed by known coordinates. Since gcd(q,2^a)=1 for odd q, equality of two residues is equivalent to equality of v modulo q. Injectivity for 2^s consecutive integers requires q>=2^s. The least odd q>=2^s (s>=1) is 2^s+1. QED.

Saturation after a bounded number of missed updates depends on the count k of *known* old coordinates: partial baseline uncertainty consumes part of the synchronization budget, and at 2r>=k even initially known coordinates cannot prevent a possible global alias.

## 4. Exact computational certificates and location sensitivity

The attached standalone integer-only JavaScript checker enumerates all ternary signed differences with <=2r nonzero coordinates outside J. For each candidate odd q below the first feasible one it records a concrete divisor witness d in D. This proves **minimality** for each finite instance, not merely that one q works. For p<=6, a separate algorithm constructs all old K-anchors and all reachable current states, and verifies both the winner and every excluded smaller odd q directly.

Coverage: p=2,...,9; r in {0,1,2}; J from empty, one low/middle/high named bit, or two low/high named bits (deduplicated, excluding the already-known/no-missed-step trivial case). This is 130 distinct parameter cases. Exact integer arithmetic; no floating-point comparisons used for the collision predicates. All assertions pass.

Selected results (minimum *odd* raw modulus q; p=6, r=1):

| uncertain old source indices J | remaining known K | volume lower bound V | exact q* | bits |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| empty | 6 | 7 | 13 | 4 |
| {0} | 5 | 12 | 43 | 6 |
| {3} | 5 | 12 | 27 | 5 |
| {5} | 5 | 12 | 43 | 6 |
| {0,1} | 4 | 20 | 53 | 6 |
| {4,5} | 4 | 20 | 59 | 6 |

At the same cardinality s=1, the **identity** of the uncertain named source changes the optimal modulus: {3} yields 27 while {0} yields 43. Thus an entropy/count-only argument is insufficient to determine the modular observation cost in this positional BRC readout.

Additional example at p=9,r=1: J=empty ->19; J={0}->89; J={4}->53; J={8}->89; J={0,1}->101; J={7,8}->109. Exact values come with per-candidate exclusion witnesses in PREFIX852_R6_PARTIAL_BASELINE_BRC_RESULTS.json.

## 5. Reproduction, limits, and research frontier

Run:
    node research_notes/portable_direct/PREFIX852_R6_PARTIAL_BASELINE_BRC_CHECK.js

The checker prints the entire JSON including 130 optimal cases and witnesses for every smaller excluded odd q. Its direct-oracle branch independently checks 79 of these cases (p<=6), reconstructing all possible anchored state sets rather than using the signed-difference theorem. Integer divisions are exact; the final bit count uses Math.log2 solely to display the integer width of small (<2^10) verified moduli.

This author-level theorem concerns a named binary **auxiliary** BRC scalar and a one-measurement resynchronization protocol. The original composite/joint relation and source metadata remain the ambient carrier; no theorem here discards history required by another future observer. It is not an admitted physical/native X6 Cell/Link/Port law, and makes no timing or physical coupling claim.

Next mathematical targets: classify q*(p,J,r) by the location/shape of J rather than its size alone; derive non-enumerative upper bounds for fixed r and arbitrary p; extend to multiple post-erasure observations and independently typed native event admissions. Existing PREFIX-851 results remain unchanged.
